key_insight: IQP quantum-kernel expressivity depends on circuit-accessible frequencies and bandwidth, benefiting learning when these align with the data’s structure.
engineering_relevance: Known periodic or multimodal data structure can guide bandwidth selection rather than assuming a high-dimensional quantum embedding will improve performance.
method: Characterize the IQP kernel’s reproducing kernel Hilbert space through Fourier representations of its generators.
Express generators as finite trigonometric sums on polynomially transformed inputs, with circuit-defined frequencies scaled by bandwidth.
Identify three bandwidth regimes: localised, multimodal, and periodic.
evidence_signal: Synthetic classification and anomaly-detection experiments reproduce all three regimes across data dimensions and feature-map configurations, with a classical Gaussian kernel as the benchmark.
watch_item: Synthetic-data results do not establish general quantum advantage or robustness on noisy quantum hardware.
paper_title: Expressivity of IQP Feature-Map Quantum Kernels via Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
